noteWriteBack.mechanism: FHIR R4 DocumentReference.Create (Clinical Notes). Plain text only, filed to an open or closed encounter. Since Feb 2025 (May 2024 by special update) it can also file to a pre-charting visit, but only as preliminary.

requiredFields.docStatus: required; 'preliminary' (Epic marks the note incomplete so a clinician can review/edit and sign) or 'final' (default; maps to 'signed' in Epic). Pre-charting notes must be preliminary.
requiredFields.type: required; LOINC (http://loinc.org) or org-specific note type (system urn:oid:<Note Type OID>). Cannot create Discharge Instructions or Patient Instructions note types.
requiredFields.subject: required; Patient reference
requiredFields.content[0].attachment.data: required; base64; 'The decoded content must be plain text; it cannot be RTF or HTML.' Only the first attachment is saved.
requiredFields.context.encounter: required; 'This must be a clinical encounter that can hold a note. This encounter must belong to the subject.'
requiredFields.author: shown in the example (Practitioner reference); not marked required in the create table

noteWriteBack.loincNote: 'Epic organizations can map additional LOINC codes to note types as well.'
noteWriteBack.quote: DocumentReference.Create (Clinical Notes) is used to file a plain text clinical note to an open (in progress) encounter or to a closed (finalized) encounter in the patient's chart. ... contentType: Content type. This must be "text/plain". ... Documents marked "preliminary" are given an incomplete status in Epic so that a clinician can review or edit the document before signing it in Epic.
noteWriteBack.firstAvailableVersion: August 2020 (products: EpicCare Ambulatory Base, EpicCare Inpatient Base)
noteWriteBack.alternative: Epic's spec names the HL7v2 Incoming MDM (Transcriptions) interface as the alternative: it can create rich text notes, interact with In Basket, create encounters on the fly and fuzzy-match encounters.

Condition.detail: Condition.Create (Problems) (R4), POST api/FHIR/R4/Condition. Items go to a holding tank; a provider must reconcile them into the problem list. Duplicate checks run.

AllergyIntolerance.detail: AllergyIntolerance.Create (Patient Chart) (R4). Goes to a holding tank until a clinician reconciles it.

Observation.detail: Observation.Create (Vital Signs) (R4) files one value to a vitals-mapped flowsheet row. It must match an existing Encounter FHIR ID and cannot write to closed encounters or future appointments. Observation.Create (Flowsheets) (R4) covers other flowsheet rows (api=49210).

ehrs.noteStructureConventions: Notes are typed by Epic note type. Epic-released note types carry a LOINC code, an org-specific Note Type category (system ending 7.4.737880.5010) and an Epic-released category (urn:oid:1.2.840.114350.1.72.727879.69848980). Organization-specific note types may only have local codings. Notes have statuses (preliminary/incomplete vs signed/final, amended) and can link SmartData Elements, problems and orders through context.related. Read-back content comes as text/html and text/rtf Binary attachments. Section-level conventions (SmartText/SmartPhrase templates) are not documented on the public pages reviewed (unverified).

requiredFields.subject: required; Patient reference only

requiredFields.content.attachment.contentType: required; must include MIME type AND charset. Supported: application/pdf, text/plain;charset=utf-8, text/richtext;charset=utf-8, text/rtf;charset=utf-8, text/html;charset=utf-8, application/xml;charset=utf-8, application/xhtml+xml;charset=utf-8

noteWriteBack.mechanism: Two documented paths in the Greenfield US Core STU7 API docs. (1) Section-level narrative: POST Observation with the EHR-specific 'document' category writes text into a section of an in-process document, identified by the HPI/ROS/PE/A&P LOINC code. It returns 202 Accepted and is held until the applicable user reviews and approves it. (2) Whole-document: POST DocumentReference is listed ('This method allows for storage of a DocumentReference resource. The body should be DocumentReference resource and the id will be missing from the resource.'), with scopes user/DocumentReference.write and patient/DocumentReference.write. Required fields and content types for (2) are not documented on the public page (unverified). Note: MEDITECH's marketing page still calls the US Core APIs 'view-only'. Suki markets its integration as using 'MEDITECH Expanse Documentation APIs'.

Observation (Documentation Text).subject: must be provided with the applicable Patient reference
Observation (Documentation Text).encounter: must be provided with the applicable Encounter reference
Observation (Documentation Text).focus: Identifier-based reference to the in-process document: {"identifier": {"value": "{{identifier for the document}}", "system": "https://{{host}}/identifier/document"}}
Observation (Documentation Text).code: LOINC: 10164-2 HPI Narrative - Reported; 10187-3 ROS Narrative - Reported; 29545-1 Physical Findings - Narrative; 51847-2 Assessment/Plan
Observation (Documentation Text).performer: conditionally required if the Practitioner can't be determined from the auth context
Observation (Documentation Text).response: 202 Accepted; Content-Location header gives the expected future Observation ID

noteWriteBack.quote: If the data is accepted, a 202 status code will be returned; acknowledging acceptance of the data. The Observation instance will not be immediately available; as it must first be reviewed and approved by the applicable user. ... Since in-process documentation is not currently available via FHIR APIs, an EHR specific Identifier value is used for referencing the documentation that the text is relevant to
noteWriteBack.openQuestion: How a third party gets the in-process document identifier (the focus) is not explained on the public page (unverified).

noteWriteBack.mechanism: Not through FHIR: the R4 CapabilityStatement lists DocumentReference as read and search-type only. Notes are written section by section into an OPEN encounter with the proprietary athenaOne chart APIs (HPI, ROS, Physical Exam, Assessment). Outside-care documents go up with the clinical document endpoint. These are non-Certified APIs, so production needs a Platform Services contract.
noteWriteBack.endpoint: PUT /v1/{practiceid}/chart/encounter/{encounterid}/hpi ; PUT /v1/{practiceid}/chart/encounter/{encounterid}/reviewofsystems ; PUT /v1/{practiceid}/chart/encounter/{encounterid}/physicalexam ; Assessment section (assessmenttext + replacetext; exact path not opened, likely /chart/encounter/{encounterid}/assessment, unverified) ; POST /v1/{practiceid}/patients/{patientid}/documents/clinicaldocument

requiredFields.prerequisite: encounterid of an OPEN encounter (set when the patient checks in). Sources: GET /chart/{patientid}/encounters, GET /appointments/booked, appointments/changed subscription, or Embedded App launch context.
requiredFields.ROS / Physical Exam: GET first with showstructured=true. PUT back templateids and put the narrative in sectionnote; replacesectionnote true=replace, false=append.
requiredFields.HPI: GET with showstructured=true, then PUT sectionnote + the full hpi array + the full templatedata array + replacesectionnote. 'anything you don't pass in will be removed.'
requiredFields.sectionnote format: Light HTML is accepted. athena: 'This HTML formatting has only been tested for these encounter sections: Assessment, ROS, PE, HPI.' athena 'strongly recommend[s]' labeling API-imported text.
requiredFields.clinicaldocument: departmentid (required), documentsubclass (required), attachmentcontents (base64; encrypted PDFs not supported; under 20MB recommended), attachmenttype, documentdata (text), autoclose (skip clinical inbox), internalnote, providerid. For care NOT provided by the practice.

noteWriteBack.loincNote: The section APIs take no LOINC codes. For read-back, athena's US Core DocumentReference returns LOINC types; a third-party summary of athena docs lists 11488-4, 11506-3, 28570-0, 34117-2 (thirdPartySource: https://nirmitee.io/blog/fhir-documentreference-clinical-notes-epic-oracle-athenahealth/).
noteWriteBack.quote: The Assessment section is the simplest among all chart sections for adding notes. It requires only the encounterid, the assessmenttext (note field), and a parameter indicating whether to replace text (replacetext = yes or no). ... always make the GET call before the PUT call so you don't override anything in the template that the provider may have documented.
noteWriteBack.hpiQuote: It is extremely important to note that anything you pass in will become the new HPI. Even if you only wish to make an addition, you will need to pass in the whole output of the GET plus your addition, otherwise anything you don't pass in will be removed.

Encounter.detail: PUT /v1/{practiceid}/chart/encounter/{encounterid} updates only patientlocationid and patientstatusid.

ehrs.noteStructureConventions: The athenaOne encounter is organized into chart sections, each with its own API. HPI, Review of Systems and Physical Exam are template-driven (practice-configured templates of paragraphs, sentences and findings with dropdown options) plus a free-text 'sectionnote'. Assessment takes free-text 'assessmenttext'. Read-back can be structured JSON (showstructured=true) or 'lightly-HTML marked up English text, as displayed in the athenanet encounter summary'. Physical Exam is renamed Mental Health Exam for behavioral health specialties.
